response_content: {"selected_paradigms": ["clique_density", "spectral", "homophily_violation", "community"], "rationale": "clique_density shows the sharpest tail of any landmarker (p50=0.009 -> p99=0.502, ~56x), matching the graph's high clustering_coeff=0.33 combined with a power-law, hub-heavy degree distribution (max_degree=1881, degree_std=131.5) -- a small set of nodes sit in abnormally dense triangle-closure regions typical of injected cliques/collusion rings; its own description flags it as the structural companion for sparse high-dim graphs, and feature_dim=12047 at 99.75% sparsity matches exactly. spectral has the largest separation in std terms (mean=0.066, p99=0.638, ~6 std above mean), and spectral_gap=0.9922 means the graph's low-frequency structure is tightly clustered, so the minority high-frequency nodes stand out sharply -- a mechanism orthogonal to triangle closure. homophily_violation is supported by a moderate global homophily=0.5334 (a real mixed population, not uniformly homophilous or heterophilous) plus a heavy per-node tail (p99=0.692 vs mean=0.126), giving a content-vs-structure view complementary to the two structural signals. community is supported by only moderate modularity=0.2432 over 10 communities despite strong overall clustering, with a heavy-tailed residual (p99=0.652 vs p50=0.0999), indicating a subset of nodes poorly fit their assigned community. local_affinity was excluded despite being in the catalog: its distribution is saturated at ceiling (p50=0.992, p90=p95=p99=1.0, std=0.038) with no separation, almost certainly an artifact of the extreme feature sparsity (0.9975) rather than a real signal."}
